subtopics.title: What Internal Control Is — and What It Protects

questions.question: Which option states all four objectives of internal control?
options: Maximise profit, reduce tax, satisfy customers, reward staff
Safeguard assets, ensure accurate and reliable records, promote efficient operations, encourage adherence to policies
Prevent all errors, eliminate all fraud, remove all waste, punish offenders
Record transactions, post to ledgers, balance the books, prepare statements

questions.question: Stock expiring unsold on a forgotten shelf is an example of which enemy of the business?
options: Fraud
Error
Waste
Collusion

questions.question: Why does division of duties make fraud harder?
options: Because it doubles the number of staff a business must employ
Because fraud attempted alone must then slip past a second, independent pair of eyes, and collusion is rarer and riskier than private temptation
Because it guarantees that no employee will ever be tempted
Because one person working alone always makes more errors

subtopics.title: The Five Components of Internal Control

questions.question: The owner helps herself to till cash for the weekend, while a procedure on the wall forbids exactly that. Which component is being destroyed?
options: Monitoring
The control environment — the tone at the top
Risk assessment
Information systems and communication

questions.question: A business sits down and lists where cash changes hands and where stock could disappear. Which component is this?
options: Risk assessment
Control activities
Monitoring
The control environment

questions.question: Why does a rule 'nobody was told about' control nothing?
options: Because unwritten rules are illegal in a business
Because controls only work when accurate information reaches the people who must act on it — the information and communication component
Because staff always ignore rules that are written down
Because rules must be approved by the bank before they apply

questions.question: Surprise cash counts and the annual stocktake compared against the records belong to which component, and why?
options: Control activities, because counting is a physical safeguard
Risk assessment, because counting identifies new dangers
Monitoring, because someone is verifying that the controls work in practice, not only on paper
The control environment, because managers do the counting

questions.question: What is the two-fold purpose of numbered source documents?
options: They look professional and impress customers
They provide evidence for the records, and the number sequence itself is a control — a missing number demands an answer
They replace the need for journals and ledgers entirely
They allow the business to claim VAT and reduce its tax

questions.question: 'Cash in a safe, banked daily and intact; the storeroom locked with named keyholders.' Which control activity is this?
options: Authorisation
Independent checks
Physical safeguards
Division of duties

questions.question: Why is comparing the bank statement with the cash journals an effective control?
options: Because the bank always corrects the business's arithmetic
Because two independently created records that must agree will expose an error or theft the moment they disagree
Because the bank statement legally overrides the journals
Because it saves the business from doing a stocktake

subtopics.title: Reading a Scenario Like an Examiner

questions.question: What are the three moves of a full internal-control scenario answer?
options: Identify the weakness, explain the risk, recommend the control
Name the component, define it, give an example
Quote the definition, list the objectives, name the documents
Blame the employee, calculate the loss, inform the owner

questions.question: At Zwane Building Supplies one clerk orders the cement, signs for deliveries and pays the suppliers. What is the weakness, in control language?
options: Poor risk assessment — cement is a high-risk product
No division of duties — one person controls the entire purchasing cycle
No physical safeguards — cement is left outside
No documentation — cement orders cannot be written down

questions.question: Why does the recommendation 'the owner should supervise more closely' earn nothing?
options: Because owners are not allowed to supervise their staff
Because it is vague — a recommendation must be specific, actionable and aimed at the exact weakness, like separating ordering from receiving
Because supervision is a monitoring issue, not a control activity
Because the owner is always the person committing the fraud

questions.question: The float is short on Friday and Bongani ran everything alone with no records. Why can nobody — including Bongani — prove what happened?
options: Because the teacher failed to watch him every break
Because with one person, no records and no counting, honesty and theft leave exactly the same evidence: none
Because tuck-shop money legally belongs to the school
Because chips are too cheap for the losses to be traced

questions.question: In the replayed week, Zanele takes the money, Bongani passes out stock, and Karabo ticks each sale. Which principle is now at work?
options: Division of duties
Authorisation
Risk assessment
Monitoring

questions.question: How does the improved system PROTECT Bongani?
options: It stops him from ever touching the stock again
When the counted box matches the tick sheet, his honesty becomes provable instead of a matter of hope
It transfers all blame to Zanele and Karabo if money goes missing
It lets him keep the float in his blazer pocket safely

subtopics.title: Five Questions Every Business Must Answer

questions.question: 'The teacher in charge borrows from the cash box till Monday.' Which plain question — and formal component — does this moment betray?
options: Who sets the example? — the control environment
What could go wrong? — risk assessment
What rules stop it? — control activities
Who checks the checkers? — monitoring

questions.question: Friday's team briefs Monday's team on what was decided, using the tick sheet and counting page. Which component is working?
options: Risk assessment
Monitoring
Information systems and communication
The control environment

questions.question: The treasurer springs a surprise count at break. Which plain question is being answered?
options: What rules stop it?
Who checks that the rules still happen?
Who sets the example?
Does everyone know what's happening?

subtopics.title: Spot the Weakness — Your Turn on Patrol

questions.question: The car-wash owner's brother takes all Saturday payments, buys supplies from the money bag, and pays his own wage from it. What is the core weakness?
options: The brother is paid too much for weekend work
One person holds every role, and wages are self-served from uncounted, unrecorded cash
Soap and polish should never be bought on a Saturday
The car wash lacks an asset register for its equipment

questions.question: The storeroom door is propped open all morning on delivery days. Which control closes the gap?
options: The owner should trust the delivery drivers more
Deliveries should be stopped on busy mornings
Keep the storeroom locked; one named person receives and counts each delivery against the delivery note before anything is shelved
Install brighter lights in the storeroom

questions.question: Receipts are written on loose, unnumbered slips only when a customer asks. Why does a numbered duplicate receipt book fix this?
options: Numbered books are cheaper than loose paper in the long run
A receipt for every sale makes income complete, and the number sequence becomes a watchdog — any gap in the numbers asks its own question
Customers prefer receipts that carry a printed number
Duplicate books remove the need to record sales in the journals
